newsitem.title: USA: Toyota tries to block Republic purchase.
newsitem.headline: Toyota tries to block Republic purchase.

text.p: Toyota Motor Sales U.S.A. said Wednesday it has asked the Texas Motor Vehicle Board to block the sale of a Houston Toyota dealership to Republic Industries Inc., the fast-growing megadealer controlled by Florida billionaire Wayne Huizenga.

Toyota, in one of the first open clashes between a major automaker and Republic, said the sale would harm the public interest and threaten the Japanese automaker's marketplace representation. Toyota Motor Sales U.S.A. is the U.S. arm of Toyota Motor Corp.
Toyota said Republic's proposed purchase of Joe Myers Toyota in Houston violates the company's required nine-month waiting period between acquisitions.
In February, Rebublic bought Kendall Toyota and Kendall Lexus, both in Florida. Lexus is Toyota's luxury division. Toyota did not oppose those purchases, said Toyota spokesman Bob Wade.

Republic has also refused to sign Toyota's Public Entity Agreement in conjunction with its proposed purchase of Joe Myers Toyota. The agreement spells out the waiting requirements Toyota requires from dealers.

Wade said current company policy limits one owner to seven Toyota division dealerships nationally, and has other restrictions for common ownership in a given sales region. For Lexus, the company limits owners to three dealerships on a national basis, and two in a region.

According to Toyota, Republic has informed the automaker it intends to buy 59 Toyota dealerships within the next 18 months, which could represent up to 20 percent of the annual sales of Toyota brand vehicles in the United States.
Republic's stock fell $4.44 to $27.25 on Nasdaq in early afternoon trading.
